newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Higher interest rates boost Philippine peso.
newsitem.headline: Higher interest rates boost Philippine peso.

text.p: Higher domestic interest rates pushed up the Philippine peso on Tuesday to close at 26.255 pesos to the dollar from 26.281, traders said.
Traders sold dollars to shift to peso-denominated assets after the Central Bank moved up its overnight lending rate to 15 from 13 percent.
"It was more of an interest play," said a dealer.
Traders said the Central Bank raised its lending rate to encourage banks with excess pesos to lend and assuage the tightness caused by covering of weekend positions for four days.
But the Central Bank's absence in the market sent the peso to a day-high of 26.252. The Bank eventually emerged in late trades, buying dollars at 26.255 pesos.

"I would like to be mysterious. We will allow the peso to appreciate, but we will intervene at the right level," Central Bank treasury head Sergio Edeza told reporters, when asked why he withdrew his buying level which was at 26.282 on Monday.
One dealer estimated the Central Bank bought about $43 million.
The day's average was at 26.264 pesos to the dollar compared with 26.283 on Monday. Volume was higher at $182.60 million from $151.10 million.
